sections.heading: Lo + adjective + que: how …
sections.body:
*Lo* + adjective / adverb + *que* expresses intensity — "how (very)…" — and the adjective agrees with the noun:

*No sabes lo difícil que es.* (You don't know how hard it is.)
*Me sorprendió lo rápido que habla.* (I was surprised at how fast he talks.)
*Mira lo guapa que está tu hija.* (Look how pretty your daughter looks.)
*Es increíble lo caras que son las casas.* (It's incredible how expensive the houses are.)

sections.heading: Lo + adjective as a noun
sections.body: You learned *lo bueno, lo malo, lo importante*. It extends to any adjective: *lo nuevo* (what's new), *lo extraño* (the strange thing), *lo curioso es que…* (the funny/curious thing is that…), *lo de…* (the thing about…, the matter of…): *¿Te enteraste de lo de Juan?* (Did you hear about what happened with Juan?) *Lo de ayer fue increíble.*

sections.heading: El hecho de que
sections.body: *El hecho de que* (the fact that) usually takes the **subjunctive**, even for real facts, because the fact is presented as a topic to comment on: *El hecho de que no haya llamado me preocupa.* *El hecho de que seas joven no significa que no tengas razón.* With *debido al hecho de que* or when the fact is clearly asserted, the indicative is also possible.

sections.heading: Infinitives as nouns
sections.body: The infinitive works as a noun (English "-ing"), sometimes with *el*: *(El) fumar es malo para la salud.* (Smoking is bad for your health.) *Me encanta cocinar.* *El saber no ocupa lugar.* (Knowledge takes up no space — proverb.)

vocab: the matter of / what happened with
to hear about / find out about
